transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Hurst.
The State Department says it's moving some diplomats
out of the Middle East amid new concerns about possible attacks
from Iran and ongoing threats from the Houthis in Yemen.
And here's Michelle Kellerman has more.
>> The Director of National Intelligence, Jay Clayton,
says the administration has received information
that Iran has "substantially increased efforts
to target U.S. personnel."
He tells Secretary of State Marco Rubio in a memo
that the plots have reached advanced stages
in both the Middle East and certain other countries.
The State Department confirmed the unclassified memo and said
that the new intelligence is informing staffing adjustments
at its embassies.
Earlier this week, some diplomats
and family members were evacuated from the U.S. Embassy
in Saudi Arabia because of attacks from Yemen.
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News.
>> Former President Obama is on the campaign trail
in Ohio and Michigan today.
He's rallying for Democrats ahead
of the midterm elections, which are less than two weeks away.
President Trump, meanwhile, is campaigning
for Republican candidates in Georgia again today.
Tomorrow, he heads back to Michigan.
President Trump says he's the one
who told the Justice Department to sue Alaska preemptively
if the Republican candidate doesn't win because he
and another candidate have the same name.
The State Supreme Court allowed both men on the ballot.
And here's Ron Elving has more.
>> We see Trump, in his first term, getting angry with people
in his Justice Department who have pushed back
on some of his orders.
People who chose to follow the law in previous policy.
Trump has since tried to get rid of those people
and replace them with lawyers who will do what he wants.
So there are many who fear what might be next
if Trump isn't pleased with the election results 10 days
from now in places other than Alaska.
>> And here's Ron Elving reporting.
Cyber criminal threat is a major source of fraud
in the Federal Food Assistance Program, known as SNAP.
Now, the Trump administration is proposing
that all 50 states bolster the program's security features
on the cards that are used to buy groceries.
And here's Juliana Kim has more.
>> Most food assistance cards are not chip-enabled,
which is the standard for most debit and credit cards today.
Cards with chips are better at protecting against a form
of theft known as card skimming, where a device can steal data.
States have been slow to upgrade largely because it's expensive.
As a result, SNAP recipients have lost millions
of dollars over the years.
The Food and Nutrition Administration's new proposed
rule would require states to roll out chips
within a certain time frame.
This change is something that the US Department
of Agriculture's inspector general, as well as Republicans
and Democrats in Congress, have advocated for.
Juliana Kim, NPR News.
>> And you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says the speed
of the Starlink satellite system and star shield,
its military version, are operating once again
at normal speeds.
This follows a week of slower service
that hampered the country's ability
to intercept Russian drone attacks,
and it forced the cancellation of some operations.
The problems with the Elon Musk-owned system came
after President Trump made a deal
to buy Russian diesel while telling Zelensky
to stop attacking Russian oil refineries.
The Pentagon has released a new set of UFO files,
and as NPR's Jeff Brumfield reports,
it includes a recent sighting.
In June, two FBI agents at an undisclosed facility spotted
a black triangular object several miles to the west
of an observation post they were manning.
It rose up over a ridge line, hovered for several seconds,
and then shot into a nearby canyon at the speed
of a fighter jet before disappearing into the shadows.
The report says the unidentified craft was silent
and thermal imagery didn't show any signs of engine exhaust.
In recent years, the government has become increasingly
concerned about sighting some possible Chinese drones
around U.S. bases and research sites.
The origin of this specific object remains unknown,
but the truth is out there.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
-It's a volatile week on Wall Street
with all three major indices ending the day on Friday
in the red that out on 652 points,
NASDAQ down 53, S&P 500 down 39.
I'm Janine Herbst, and you're listening
to "NPR News" from Washington.

topics.text: State Department moves some diplomats out of the Middle East over Iran and Houthi threats
Obama and Trump campaign in Ohio, Michigan, and Georgia ahead of midterm elections
Trump says he told Justice Department to sue Alaska over duplicate candidate names on ballot
Trump administration proposes requiring chip-enabled SNAP cards to reduce grocery benefit fraud
Zelensky says Starlink satellite service has returned to normal speeds in Ukraine
Pentagon releases new UFO files, including a June sighting by two FBI agents
Wall Street ends volatile Friday session sharply lower, Nasdaq down 653 points
